titulo_en: I'm going to visit my family

titulo_es.@es: Going to para planes; will para decisiones
titulo_es.@en: Going to for plans; will for decisions

consejo.@es: Forma corta de «I will». Lleva apóstrofo.
consejo.@en: Short form of «I will». He's got an apostrophe.

texto.@es: Se suele usar **be going to** + verbo base para un plan que ya habías decidido: **I'm going to visit Rome** (voy a visitar Roma: ya lo tengo decidido). Se conjuga **be**: **am**, **is** o **are** + **going to**.
texto.@en: **be going to** + verbo base is usually used for a plan you had already decided: **I'm going to visit Rome** (I will visit Rome: I have it decided). **be**: **am**, **is** or **are** + **going to** is conjugated.

texto.@es: **Be going to** es muy común cuando una predicción se basa en algo que vemos ahora: **Look at the clouds. It's going to rain** (mira las nubes; va a llover). **Will** también puede expresar predicciones u opiniones; son pautas frecuentes y el contexto importa.
texto.@en: **Be going to** is very common when a prediction is based on something we see now: * * Look at the clouds. It's going to rain * * (look at the clouds; it's going to rain). **Will** can also express predictions or opinions; they are frequent patterns and the context matters.

texto.@es: Cuando decides en ese momento, suele usarse **will**: **I'll get an umbrella** (cogeré un paraguas). También se usa **will** para ofrecer ayuda: **I'll help you** (te ayudaré).
texto.@en: When you decide at that time, you usually use **will**: **I'll get an umbrella** (I will take an umbrella). **will** is also used to offer help: **I'll help you** (I will help you).

intro.@es: Compara dos usos habituales del futuro: **going to** para planes o predicciones basadas en señales presentes, y **will** para decisiones del momento y ofertas.
intro.@en: Compare two usual future uses: **going to** for plans or predictions based on present signals, and **will** for current decisions and offers.
